material.notes: Audit 13 downgrade. Own comparer (sheet cells from the cell order, best placement within 3 px, every pixel of the cell compared, text and icon ink set apart by the -notext twin): the flat-pixel metric of round 23 sees 0 off because a 2 px outline is never flat, but the unchecked box in hover, focus and pressed draws its outline in on-surface-variant (#49454F) where Material Web draws on-surface (#1D1B20; its checkbox-styles.css sets hover-outline-color to on-surface, and the M3 spec agrees): 116 to 124 px per state off by up to 47 levels (light and dark), 3 states. Everything else in the sheet is within the rim noise of two anti-aliasers.
gaps: The error check box is the M3 error tokens applied to Material Web's element (the library defines them but draws no error state)
Evidence: Material Web 1.x rendered in Chromium (focus is the 10 % state layer, pressed 10 %, M3 tracking set to zero as Neper's text engine has no letter spacing); no Android device capture
Unchecked checkbox outline in hover, focus and pressed must be on-surface, not on-surface-variant

material.notes: Audit 13 downgrade. The app bar reference is not a Material Web capture: Material Web has no top app bar, so scripts/material/gallery.html draws it as plain HTML and CSS written from the M3 specification by the same hand that wrote Neper's. A pixel match against it proves two readings of the spec agree, not that Neper matches a real control; matched needs a capture. My comparer agrees with the claim as far as it goes (title 1 px shift in the no-leading cell, 47 px).
gaps: Material Web has no app bar: the reference is plain CSS from the specification
Medium and large app bars are not compared
Evidence: Material Web 1.x rendered in Chromium (focus is the 10 % state layer, pressed 10 %, M3 tracking set to zero as Neper's text engine has no letter spacing); no Android device capture

neper_dark.notes: Audit 13 downgrade. Independent text contrast over the sheets of neper-dark: the five hint_toolbar_* sheets draw the v3 toolbar hint, a pale yellow box (#FFFFE1) with Text (#E1E2E9) ink, 1.27:1; hint_grid_header_name draws a #F9F9F9 box with #BBC1C5 ink, 1.73:1. Both are enabled text and fail 4.5:1. hint.png itself is dark and passes (10.9:1). The Windows-only hint variants leak into the dark directory unmapped, the same cause that keeps tree list and data grid at review.
gaps: Derived from the Neper dark palette, not compared to any reference screen (there is none): started/review only, never matched
Neper dark has no reference screen: never matched; ready here means the checker's criteria hold in every state the sheet renders
hint_toolbar_* and hint_grid_header_name: light Windows hint chrome with dark-look text (1.27 and 1.73 to 1)
